title: a project cannot add checks to doctor: a project handler replaces devbin's doctor outright, so its own checks stop running
body:
## What happens

A project cannot add checks to `devbin doctor`. The only way to get project checks into `doctor` is a project handler at `bin/.devbin/cmd/doctor`, and shadowing is total (`lib/resolve`, AC-04.4): the handler replaces devbin's doctor outright, so devbin's own checks (manifest, runtime, shadowing, launcher, source, bash floor) stop running.

The workaround is for the project handler to call devbin's handler by path and then run its own checks:

    "$DEVBIN_LIB/cmd/doctor" | sed 's/^/  /'
    ... project checks ...

That works, but it reaches into `lib/`, which is devbin's side of the seam: a project that depends on `lib/cmd/doctor` existing at that path, taking no arguments and exiting non-zero on failure is depending on devbin internals that no contract promises. It also gives two summaries (devbin's "11 checks, 0 failed" and then the project's own count), and doctor's shadowing check reports the result as "doctor shadows the built-in", a note about a design the project did not want.

## How it was found

Building `intranet doctor` in the Intranet project (`~/Dropbox/Sinclair-Shared/Intranet`, devbin 0.1.1 vendored), 2026-09-19. The Intranet has tools, config, SSH access to several machines, a network-switch state and 1Password access that its commands rely on, and `doctor` is the natural home for checking them. The handler is `bin/.devbin/cmd/doctor` there; it uses the workaround above.

## Why it matters

`doctor` is the command a person runs when something is wrong, so it is where a project's preconditions belong: tools on PATH, config present and parseable, remotes reachable, credentials available. Today a project has to choose between losing devbin's checks and reaching into `lib/`. Every devbin project that grows real preconditions will make the same choice, and each will write its own copy of the workaround (the four-launchers problem devbin was folded to end).

## Shape of a fix (not prescribed)

A way for a project to contribute checks that devbin's doctor runs after its own, with one summary. For example, executables in `bin/.devbin/cmd/doctor.d/`, each printing devbin's own `ok` / `FAIL` / `note` lines and exiting non-zero on failure, with doctor counting them into its total and exiting 1 if any failed. Whatever the mechanism, it should be discovered (no config edit to register a check, as with `cmd/`), keep devbin's checks running first, and leave a total shadow of `doctor` available for a project that genuinely wants one.


## Fix

`c842095` (vc; reviewed by dc, passed). Every executable in a project's `bin/.devbin/cmd/doctor.d/` runs after devbin's own checks, counted into the one summary, and `devbin doctor <check>` runs one alone. The directory is `cmd/<name>.d/` by hv's choice (2026-09-19): it's where a word under a command already lives. A line whose first word is `ok`, `FAIL` or `note` counts as devbin's own do, and other output is shown as detail. The exit status counts too, and neither hides the other: a non-zero exit with no FAIL line fails, naming the exit, and a FAIL line fails even at exit 0. A non-executable file there is a note, not run. The handlers check knows `doctor.d` is doctor's. A total shadow at `cmd/doctor` still works. Declared at the site: a check is not time-limited, so one that reaches another machine should bound itself. Documented in `docs/authoring-commands.md` ("Checks of your own in doctor") and `help/doctor.md`. Eight arms, all red first; eight self-mutants, all killed. The Intranet can move its checks into `doctor.d/` once it takes devbin's next release, and drop its workaround through `lib/`.
